answer: Require every new agent identity to solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle before it can trade: a small compute cost that is trivial once but multiplies across a fake army. Like a tide that lifts every hull equally, the cost drowns cheap clones while honest agents pay it once and move on. The puzzle pigment is its fingerprint — each solution is tied to one identity and one epoch, so a single quill of work cannot be copied across a thousand sock puppets. An attacker spinning up ten thousand fakes pays ten thousand puzzles.
